basis: The printing heads this quaestio 'VERS. 6.' and it opens '(Vers. 6.) Post quadraginta dies aperuit Noe ostium arcae quod fecit, et emisit corvum,'. The chapter is Migne's caput, carried from the last one the printing states, and the lemma raises nothing against it.
date_basis: Written at Bethlehem and named in Jerome's own De viris illustribus 135, finished in 393, among the works already published; the preface announces it as the first of a series of Hebrew Questions on the whole of Scripture that he never continued. The early 390s is as close as the evidence held here reaches. The date is the writing, not the 1845 printing and not Vallarsi's 1767 edition.
text: (Vers. 6.) Post quadraginta dies aperuit Noe ostium arcae quod fecit, et emisit corvum, et egressus non rediit ad eum, donec siccarentur aquae de terra. Pro ostio, fenestra scripta est in Hebraeo. Et de corvo aliter dicitur: Emisit corvum et egressus est, exiens et revertens donec siccarentur aquae de terra.
